episodes.166249: An area of pre-frontal thunderstorms developed in the early morning hours and moved north across the coastal waters.
episodes.166435: As a line of thunderstorms pushed over and offshore of the coast in Brevard and Indian River Counties, several strong wind gusts were observed.
episodes.166802: A slow moving cluster of thunderstorms that lasted just over an hour passed near the City of Galax and the community of Fries in the evening of the 23rd. Despite modest instability of 250-500 J/kg of surface-based CAPE, an anomalously-high precipitable water estimate of about 1.2 inches created a healthy environment for strong rainfall rates embedded in convective systems.  MRMS FLASH returns were unimpressive during this event, registering 1-hour average recurrence intervals in the 2- to 5-year range.
episodes.167176: Prefrontal showers and isolated thunderstorms moved across southeast Georgia and northeast Florida Thursday morning as a cold front was to the west of the area. Waves of upper level energy moved ahead of and along the front, continuing waves of showers and storms. Storms trained over downtown Jacksonville for most of the morning and afternoon causing street flooding and McCoy���s Creek to overflow its bank. Strong winds from passing storms also caused downed power lines in Alachua county.
episodes.167497: Numerous thunderstorms were able to form during the afternoon of March 23rd across eastern Ohio ahead of an occluded front.  Although forecasts of instability and shear were sufficiently high for the issuance of a Tornado Watch, the levels of CAPE ended up being lower than anticipated, which blunted the overall severe threat.  One instance each of hail and high winds were reported, along with a funnel cloud.
episodes.167795: Heavy rainfall combined with wet antecedent conditions resulted in flooding along portions of the Ouachita, Saline, Fourche LaFave, White, and Cache Rivers.
episodes.167812: A cold front moving across the region resulted in development of a line of scattered thunderstorms across Upstate South Carolina during the evening. A couple of the storms produced tornadoes in Pickens County, with one of those being significant.
episodes.167839: A warm front headed north into the region bringing a large swath of rain. Immediately south of the front, atmospheric conditions became unstable enough for a few storms to develop. One such storm increased enough in strength for its winds to down trees across parts of Wilkes County and one home experienced minor damage.
episodes.167843: A warm front headed north into the region bringing a large swath of rain. Immediately south of the front, atmospheric conditions became unstable enough for a few storms to develop. One storm developed with enough rotation to generate a tornado in Carroll County.
episodes.167911: Scattered thunderstorms associated with low pressure and a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of southeast Virginia.
episodes.168025: A cold front moving across the region resulted in development of a line of scattered thunderstorms over western Nouth Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced locally damaging wind gusts in addition to an EF1 tornado in  Alexander County. Additionally, heavy rainfall resulted in some localized flooding in the southern mountains.

events.narrative: An automated weather station (Weather Underground: KVAGALAX92) near the City of Galax observed a 75-minute rainfall total of 1.39 inches. This amount is estimated to be between a 2- and 5-year rainfall event per NOAA Atlas 14 point frequency estimates for this duration.
Emergency manager reported trees blown down at Roby Conley Rd and on Green St Loop.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor damage to a home near the intersection of Mount Zion Road and Shell Creek Road. Damage values are estimated.
Thunderstorm winds blew a tree down near the intersection of Congo Road and Hamby Mountain Road. Damage values are estimated.
Thunderstorm winds blew one tree down near the intersection of Route 16 and Bumgarner Lane. Damage values are estimated.

County comms reported several tributaries of the French Broad River overflowed their banks in the Brevard area after 2.5 to 4 inches of rain fell. Several roads were inundated, including Wilson Rd and Barclay Rd.
Thunderstorm winds blew on tree down near the intersection of Dehart Community Center Road and Whitley Lane. Damage values are estimated.

NWS storm survey found the path of a strong tornado that touched down on Duncan Rd near Sarah Rose Dr, where numerous trees were blown down, one of which fell on a mobile home. The tornado traveled northeast from there, continuing to blow down numerous trees as it crossed Rolling Hills Rd and Mile Creek Rd. Hundreds of trees were down in this area, including trees as large a couple of feet in diameter. The tornado intensified as it moved towards Windmont Rd, which is where the worst damage was observed. Much of the roof was removed and one exterior wall collapsed on a brick house on Windmont Rd. Three occupants of this home were trapped and had to be rescued, with minor injuries. The tornado weakened as it continued northeast, crossing Mt Bethel Rd, Shady Grove Rd, and Reece Mill Rd before intensifying again in the area between Reece Mill Rd and Lost Valley Road, where a mobile home was split in two and rolled over off of its foundation on Crystal Ln and hundreds of trees were downed. The tornado weakened a bit but continued to blow down numerous trees northeast of there, crossing Nine Times Rd and Meece Mill Rd before lifting near Gravley Rd.

An employee of a country store/gas station reported that a clogged drainage ditch across the road caused water to overflow across the gas station parking lot and into the store up to 3 inches deep.  The water receded quickly after the rain ended, however some merchandise was damaged by the water and could not be sold.
NWS storm survey found the path of a weak, brief tornado that touched down on the shore of Lake Keowee at Mile Creek Park. A few trees were uprooted and several large branches broken.

A tornado touched down along Kinzer Road four miles east-southeast of Gladesboro, VA. The tornado traveled northeast along Gladesboro Road toward Football Lane before lifting south of U.S. Highway 58. Numerous trees were snapped and two structures were damaged along the tornado path. The one structure was a two story family home that was shifted off its foundation and had its roof torn off along Gladesboro Road. Additionally, a modular home along Football Lane had its roof partially blown off. Damage values are estimated. There was $255,000 in damage to the two damage structures, $45,000 in roof damages and approximately $100,000 in replacement costs for outbuilding structures.

A stream gauge reported flooding developed along Mud Creek after 3 to 4 inches of rain fell in the Hendersonville area in about a 24-hour period. Impacted roads included an access road at the intersection of S Church St and S Main St and Kanuga Rd at Erkwood Dr.

County comms reported trees and power lines blown down throughout the Morganton area, including at the intersection Of Propst Rd and Highway 64, and Sanford Rd at Tate St, and on Lenoir Rd and Kirksey Dr.

NWS storm survey found the path of an EF1 tornado that began with tree damage near Hidden Valley Rd just north of Gus Pennell Lane. The tornado moved northeast, crossing Lambert Fork Rd and All Healing Springs Rd, Archie Mountain Lane, Gil Childers Rd, and Dandelion Dr. Damage was primarily confined to snapped small trees and large limbs, uprooted larger trees, and a couple of destroyed outbuildings along this section of the path, although minor roof damage occurred to at least one frame home and the porch was removed from a manufactured home on Dandelion Dr. The tornado continued northeast uprooting or snapping numerous trees as it crossed the Lower Little River along Mount Olive Church Rd, roughly paralleling Mount Olive Church Rd before lifting around Russell Gap Rd.
Heavy rain brought minor river flooding to the Ouachita River at Camden.

Numerous roads were flooded in the Denbigh area to Fort Eustis. A few vehicles were stranded in high water near Denbigh Boulevard.
Heavy rain brought minor river flooding to the Ouachita River at Thatcher Lock and Dam. This point remained above flood stage through the remainder of the month.
Thunderstorm wind caused damage to powerlines along NW US Hwy 441 which led to the closure of US 441 northbound near High Springs due to crews trying to repair the powerlines.
Thunderstorm wind knocked down powerlines onto CR-235 at the intersection of CR-235 and 5th Ave in Newberry. This led to the closure of CR-235 at this intersection.
